issues.legal_issue: A female relative’s right to share when joint family property passes by survivorship to a sole surviving coparcener does not depend on an assumed partition between that coparcener and the last predeceased coparcener.
material_facts: On the death of a coparcener, the joint family property passed by survivorship to his sole surviving grandson.
The claimant was a widow of the deceased coparcener and sought a share in the property.
The trial court decreed the claim, and the High Court upheld the decree.
issues.conclusion: The right under section 8(1)(d) is independent of a partition and does not require an assumed partition to identify the females entitled to shares. The claimant was entitled to a share as the widow of a coparcener.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 8(1)(d) of the Hindu Law Women’s Rights Act, 1933, when joint family property passes by survivorship to a single coparcener, the reference to the female classes in section 8(1)(a), (b) and (c) identifies the females entitled to shares; it does not require a hypothetical partition. Section 8(3) extends the provisions relating to a mother to paternal grandmothers and great-grandmothers and includes a stepmother within “mother”; section 8(2) governs the shares. The Court approved Dakshinamurthy v. Subbamma, Venkatachaliah v. Ramalingiah and Kolla Narasinha Setty v. Nanjamma.

predicates.claim_for_share_after_survivorship: A female relative brought a claim for a share after joint family property passed by survivorship to a sole surviving coparcener.
predicates.property_passed_to_sole_survivor_by_surv: The joint family property passed by survivorship to one sole surviving coparcener.
predicates.claimant_is_widow_of_deceased_coparcener: The claimant was the widow of a deceased coparcener whose interest formed part of the joint family property.

issues.definition: When a female relative claims after property passes by survivorship to a sole surviving coparcener and she is the widow of a deceased coparcener, she is entitled to a share.
